## What's Changed

`0.75.0` changes how `coco commit --split` works: it now shows the plan and asks before committing, instead of requiring a separate `--apply` step. The release also ships a refreshed marketing site homepage and a set of purpose-built GIF recipes for consistent visual assets. **No breaking changes** for existing workflows: `--plan` preserves the old plan-only behavior, and `--apply` still skips confirmation for scripting.

## Highlights

### `--split` plans and prompts to apply in one step

- `coco commit --split` generates the split plan, prints it, then prompts "Apply these N commits? (Y/n)" with a default of yes. One command takes you from a messy staging area to clean, grouped commits.
- `--plan` is the explicit opt-out: print the plan without prompting or touching git state. Useful for reviewing a plan before deciding.
- `--apply` remains unchanged: skip the confirmation prompt entirely, for CI pipelines or scripted workflows.
- The TUI workstation's split flow (`S` in compose) is unaffected. It already has its own preview-then-confirm pattern.

## Under the hood

- Flag descriptions updated: `--split` ("shows the plan and prompts to apply"), `--plan` ("plan-only mode"), `--apply` ("apply without confirmation").

## Breaking Changes

None. `--plan` preserves the previous `--split` behavior (plan-only, no state changes). `--apply` continues to skip confirmation. Existing scripts using either flag are unaffected.

body:
## What's Changed

`0.74.0` is a workstation-correctness patch — the "the TUI tells the truth" release. Three bugs in `coco ui` let the display drift out of sync with the real repo state: the commit graph froze after git operations run outside coco, arrow keys drove the wrong panel on the Status view, and generating a PR body could corrupt the screen. All three are fixed. The rest is dependency upkeep and making coco's `.kiro/` steering files and specs public in the repo. **No breaking changes** — every command and the `coco ui` workstation behave exactly as before, only more reliably.

## Highlights — a workstation that stays in sync

### The history graph refreshes after external git operations

Running `git reset`, `rebase`, `cherry-pick`, `merge`, `commit --amend`, or `pull --rebase` in another terminal while `coco ui` was open left the commit graph pinned to its pre-operation state. The staged/worktree panel updated correctly, but the graph rows never reloaded, so the history you saw no longer matched the repo ([#1329](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1329)).

The `full` refresh path reloaded branches, tags, and metadata but skipped the history rows — diverging from the manual `r` refresh, which reloads both. `full` events now reload the graph too, and coco watches `.git/logs/HEAD` as a second signal for graph-mutating operations on the attached branch (where the symbolic `.git/HEAD` ref never changes). The graph stays current without a manual refresh.

### Arrow keys respect the focused panel on the Status view

On the Status surface, `↑`/`↓` always moved the center worktree file list — even when the left sidebar was the focused panel (its border highlighted). Navigating branches, tags, stashes, or worktrees from the sidebar was impossible without the arrows jumping the wrong list ([#1330](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1330), closes [#1328](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/issues/1328)).

The `↑`/`↓` handlers now check `focus === 'commits'` before claiming the keypress, so when the sidebar is focused they fall through to the sidebar's branch/tag/stash/worktree navigation — matching the guard the `��`/`→` group-jump handlers already used.

### Generating a PR body no longer garbles the workstation

Drafting a PR body (or a changelog) from inside `coco ui` could render a garbled inspector panel and hand `gh pr create` an empty `--title=` / `--body=` ([#1331](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1331), closes [#1327](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/issues/1327)).

The root cause was a helper that monkey-patched `process.stdout.write` to capture changelog output. During the 5–15s LLM call it also captured Ink's live spinner frames (every 80ms), filling the buffer with ANSI and box-drawing escape sequences — which then rendered back as panel content, and whose control bytes polluted the parsed title and body. The changelog generator is now a pure core function (`generateChangelogResult`) that returns its result without ever touching `process.stdout`; the PR-body and changelog TUI workflows call it with a silent logger. Regression tests assert `process.stdout.write` is never patched during either flow.

## Under the hood

- **`.kiro/` is now public** — coco's steering files (`product.md`, `structure.md`, `tech.md`, `release-notes-style.md`), the `www-site-redesign` spec, two hooks, and a root `AGENTS.md` are tracked in the repo so the project's architecture and conventions are visible, not just described ([#1324](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1324)).
- **Docs** — streamlined README (tighter intro, command table linked to the wiki) and a steering-file refresh (theme count to 128, Bitbucket added to the multi-forge line).
- **Dependencies:** `@commitlint/core` 21.0.2 → 21.1.0 ([#1323](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1323)); dev: `@commitlint/types` 21.0.1 → 21.1.0 ([#1319](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1319)), `@rollup/plugin-commonjs` 29.0.2 → 29.0.3 ([#1320](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1320)), `@types/node` 25.9.3 → 26.0.1 ([#1321](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1321)), `release-it` 20.2.0 → 20.2.1 ([#1322](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1322)).

## Breaking Changes

None. `0.74.0` is behavior-preserving: the three fixes only correct cases where `coco ui` showed stale or corrupted state, and the dependency bumps are routine. Existing configs and every TUI flow are unchanged.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/gfargo/coco/compare/0.73.0...0.74.0

summary: `0.73.0` adds **Bitbucket Cloud** as coco's fourth forge — joining GitHub, GitHub Enterprise, and GitLab. `coco prs`, `coco issues`, `coco pr create`, and the full `coco ui` workstation (triage, inspe
body:
## What's Changed

`0.73.0` adds **Bitbucket Cloud** as coco's fourth forge — joining GitHub, GitHub Enterprise, and GitLab. `coco prs`, `coco issues`, `coco pr create`, and the full `coco ui` workstation (triage, inspectors, every mutating action) now work against Bitbucket repos via its REST API. No CLI binary required. The rest is dependency upkeep and a major overhaul of the screenshot/GIF pipeline for faster, smaller marketing assets. **No breaking changes.**

## Highlights

### Bitbucket Cloud forge adapter (#1315, closes #1238)

coco auto-detects Bitbucket from the `origin` remote URL (`bitbucket.org` or any host containing `bitbucket`), then authenticates via `BITBUCKET_ACCESS_TOKEN` (Bearer) or `BITBUCKET_USERNAME` + `BITBUCKET_APP_PASSWORD` (Basic). Everything routes through a thin Node `fetch` wrapper — no external CLI binary needed.

What works on Bitbucket today:

- **`coco prs`** / **`coco issues`** — list + paginate pull requests and issues, same output as GitHub/GitLab
- **`coco pr create`** — generates title + body from branch diff and opens via the Bitbucket API
- **Workstation PR triage + issue triage** — browse, inspect, and act on PRs/issues
- **14 PR mutations** — merge, approve, close, comment, requestChanges, addReviewer, plus current-branch variants
- **Issue mutations** — comment, addAssignee, close, reopen
- **Provider detection** — `detectProvider` and the `forgeHosts` config recognize Bitbucket; `forgeNouns` returns Bitbucket-specific labels for the UI

Known Bitbucket Cloud limitations (platform, not coco):
- PR labels are unsupported — `addPullRequestLabel` returns `{ ok: false }`
- `requestChanges` is implemented as a comment (no native "changes requested" state)
- `addAssignee` maps to adding a reviewer (closest equivalent)

### Screenshot pipeline overhaul (dev tooling)

The screenshot/GIF capture system got a full performance and quality pass. These are dev-tooling changes — they don't ship in the npm package — but they dramatically speed up asset generation for the marketing site and README:

- **Instant startup** — captures now use `node dist/index.js` instead of `tsx src/index.ts`, eliminating 2-3s cold-start per recipe
- **PNG optimization** — `pngquant` compresses screenshots 50-70% with no visible quality loss
- **Timing tightened** — `POST_LAUNCH_SETTLE_MS` halved (5000→2500ms), `BOOT_HIDDEN_MS` from 2200→900ms, all recipe initial sleeps 4000→2000ms
- **Per-recipe env overrides** — recipes can pin model/provider (e.g. `gpt-4o-mini` for fast commit demos)
- **`visibleCommand`** — GIF recipes show a clean `$ coco commit` typed naturally while the real command runs behind the scenes
- **Clean terminal** — alias/env setup fully hidden; no leaked paths or commands in GIF output
- **Compact README GIFs** — dedicated `readme-commit` (80×20) and `readme-workstation` (130×32) recipes sized for GitHub's renderer

## Under the hood

- **Dependencies:** `@langchain/aws` 1.3.9 → 1.4.1 (Bedrock bearer token auth, native streamEvents) ([#1307](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1307)), `@langchain/anthropic` 1.4.0 → 1.4.1 ([#1311](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1311)), `react` 19.2.6 → 19.2.7 + `@types/react` 19.2.15 → 19.2.17 ([#1308](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1308)), `rollup` 4.61.1 → 4.62.2 ([#1310](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1310)), `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` 4.6.2 → 7.1.1 (ESLint v10 support, compiler lint improvements) ([#1309](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1309)).
- **README updated** — two hero GIFs: `readme-commit` (AI commit in action) and `readme-workstation` (TUI boot + browse).

## Breaking Changes

None. `0.73.0` is additive: Bitbucket support is a new code path that only activates when the remote points at a Bitbucket host. Existing GitHub / GitLab / GHE workflows are unchanged.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/gfargo/coco/compare/0.72.3...0.73.0

## What's Changed

`0.72.3` is a robustness patch — the "coco fails gracefully now" release. A pre-launch sweep of the first-run experience turned up three rough edges where a small mistake (a typo'd config, an unexpected error, a Ctrl-C) produced a raw stack trace or a scary message instead of something actionable. All three are fixed. The rest is dependency upkeep and contributor-facing repo polish. **No breaking changes** — every command and the `coco ui` workstation behave exactly as before.

## Highlights — graceful failures

### A malformed `.coco.json` no longer crashes coco

A single JSON typo in your project config — a stray comma, an unquoted key — used to crash coco with a raw `SyntaxError` and stack trace. Worse, config loads early, so the crash bypassed every error handler and dumped a Node trace before the command even started. coco now **warns with the file, the parse error, and how to fix it**, then falls back to your other config sources (defaults / global / git / env) so the tool still runs ([#1301](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1301)).

```
[coco] Warning: could not parse .coco.json as JSON — ignoring it.
  Parse error: Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 2 (line 1 column 3)
  Fix the file's syntax (or run `coco init` to regenerate it). Other config sources still apply.
```

### No more raw stack traces — and a faster path to reporting bugs

The top-level error handler printed the raw error object (full stack) for anything that slipped past a command's own handling. It now prints a short, actionable message with a **"report a bug" link**, and keeps the full stack behind `--verbose` / `COCO_DEBUG` so a plain run stays readable while a bug report can still include the trace ([#1299](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1299)). Intentional exits (e.g. the "missing API key" guidance) pass through untouched.

### Cancelling a prompt exits cleanly

Pressing **Ctrl-C** out of `coco init` (or running it without a TTY) surfaced as `Failed to execute command / Error: User force closed the prompt`. Cancelling is a normal action, not a crash — coco now prints a tidy `Cancelled.` and exits with the conventional interrupt code, for every interactive command ([#1302](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1302)).

## Under the hood

- **Build: restored type compatibility after the `@langchain/core` bump.** The 1.1.48 update changed `StructuredOutputParser`'s inferred types (Zod 4 internals), breaking the commit-draft chain's typecheck; brought the one strict call site in line with the existing parser call-site convention ([#1300](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1300)). The runtime is unchanged.
- **Dependencies:** `ink` 7.0.5 → 7.0.6 ([#1260](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1260)), `ajv` 8.18.0 → 8.20.0 ([#1262](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1262)), `@langchain/community` 1.1.28 → 1.1.29 ([#1258](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1258)), `@langchain/core` 1.1.48 → 1.1.49 ([#1261](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1261)), `@babel/core` 7.28.0 → 7.29.7 ([#1298](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1298)), and `@types/node` (dev) 25.6.2 → 25.9.3 ([#1259](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1259)).
- **Repo: issue forms, a PR template, and a tighter CONTRIBUTING** ([#1256](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1256)) — structured bug-report / feature-request forms so incoming reports land with the context needed to act on them.

## Breaking Changes

None. `0.72.3` is behavior-preserving: the three fixes only change how coco behaves when something goes *wrong* (turning crashes and raw errors into actionable messages), and the dependency bumps are routine. Existing configs and every TUI flow are unchanged.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/gfargo/coco/compare/0.72.2...0.72.3

## What's Changed

`0.72.2` is a small maintenance release. It fixes a workstation chrome glitch (a "loading context" indicator that never cleared) and **completes the `runtime/app.ts` decomposition** (#1237) by migrating every workstation surface onto the runtime context.

## Highlights

### Fix: the "loading context" indicator no longer sticks

On launch, the workstation header could show a permanent **"loading context"** hint — even on a fully-loaded, clean repo — because three lazily-loaded context slices (the issue list, the PR triage list, and the full PR overview) were seeded as "loading" but only fetched when you actually open their view. The header's "is anything still loading?" check therefore never cleared.

They're now seeded **idle** at boot, alongside the PR overview that was already handled this way ([#1297](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1297)). The indicator clears once the initial context finishes loading, and still flashes briefly — correctly — only while you're entering the issues / PR / PR-triage views.

## Under the hood

### The `runtime/app.ts` decomposition is fully complete (#1237)

`0.72.1` finished moving the runtime's `useState` / `useEffect` clusters into dedicated hooks. `0.72.2` finishes the other half: the **surface-context migration**. Every workstation surface — all 19 main-panel views plus the detail/inspector cluster — now reads its `state` / `theme` / `context` / loading-status / dimensions from a single `LogInkRuntimeContext` instead of having those values threaded through `app.ts → dispatcher → render*Surface` as positional props.

The payoff is contributor-facing: adding a surface-wide value is now a one-line context addition rather than a change threaded through every surface signature. It's a pure refactor — the surfaces' render logic is untouched, so output is byte-identical (the 68-snapshot suite is unchanged across all five PRs).

- Foundation: grew the runtime context and added the `useSurfaceRenderContext` / `defineSurfaceComponent` helpers ([#1292](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1292)).
- Migrated in batches by shape: zero-extra surfaces ([#1293](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1293)), single-extra surfaces ([#1294](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1294)), the history surface ([#1295](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1295)), and the detail-panel cluster ([#1296](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1296)).
- Each PR was validated with `tsc` + the workstation render-snapshot suite + `eslint` + a full build, then independently reviewed for behavior preservation.

With this, **#1237 is fully closed** — `runtime/app.ts` is a thin composition root.

## Breaking Changes

None. `0.72.2` is behavior-preserving: the surface-context migration is internal (zero render-snapshot diffs), and the one fix only stops a stuck loading indicator. Existing configs and every TUI flow are unchanged.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/gfargo/coco/compare/0.72.1...0.72.2

body:
## What's Changed

`0.72.1` is a polish-and-foundation release. It smooths the **local Ollama** path so a fully-local setup works on the first try, hardens model validation and grammar downloads, and **finishes the workstation runtime decomposition** (#1237) — the internal cleanup that `0.72.0` started. The only behavior change is a small short-flag cleanup (`-t` / `-c`); see **Breaking Changes**. Everything else — every command and the `coco ui` workstation — works exactly as before.

## Highlights

### Local Ollama, smoother out of the box

Running coco fully local against Ollama no longer assumes you've already got everything wired up — coco now meets you where you are and tells you exactly what's missing.

- **`coco init`** handles a first-run Ollama setup gracefully instead of failing when the daemon or a model isn't ready yet ([#1264](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1264)).
- **`coco doctor`** runs live checks against the Ollama daemon and your installed models, so a misconfigured local setup is diagnosable in one command ([#1265](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1265)).
- When a configured Ollama model **isn't pulled yet**, coco prints an actionable hint (the exact `ollama pull` to run) rather than a raw error ([#1266](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1266)).

### Sturdier model validation & grammar downloads

- **Per-provider model validity.** Model names are now validated against the specific provider, backed by a shared map of deprecated models — so a typo or a retired model is caught early with a clear message instead of failing mid-request ([#1272](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1272)).
- **Tree-sitter grammar mirror fallback.** Syntax-highlight grammar downloads fall back to a mirror when the primary source is unreachable, so first-run highlighting setup is more reliable on flaky networks ([#1271](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1271)).

### The workstation runtime decomposition is finished (#1237)

`0.72.0` decomposed the bulk of the workstation runtime; `0.72.1` finishes the job. The remaining `useState`/`useEffect` clusters moved into dedicated, individually-tested hooks — a behavior-preserving refactor (zero render-snapshot diffs) that leaves `runtime/app.ts` a thin composition root: it wires hooks together and renders.

- This phase: **`useState` 28 → 3** (only the core reducer state and the theme-picker preview remain), `app.ts` trimmed to **~1,711 LOC**. Together with `0.72.0`, the runtime is down from its ~5,368-LOC peak.
- Extracted hooks: commit-detail, file-preview, diff syntax-highlight, bisect-candidate, history pagination, first-run onboarding, resume repaint, the worktree/stash/compare diff state, and the foundational repo-stack runtimes ([#1273](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1273), [#1275](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1275), [#1276](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1276), [#1277](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1277), [#1278](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1278), [#1279](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1279), [#1280](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1280), [#1281](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1281), [#1282](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1282)).
- New automated coverage for the submodule drill-in/out path ([#1283](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1283)).

## Notable

- **Short-flag aliases reconciled** ([#1268](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1268), fixes #1245 / #1246). Each short letter now resolves to one flag across commands: `-t` → `--tag` (changelog) and `-c` → `--conventional` (commit). The `CommitOptions` interface was also completed (`append` / `appendTicket` / `additional` are now typed, no more loose casts). **See Breaking Changes** for the flag change.
- **Workstation: no more stuck "Loading…" in the inspector.** Four lazy diff/detail loaders could leave their loading flag stuck `true` if the selection cleared mid-fetch — surfacing as a permanent "Loading commit details…" until the next selection. Fixed by resetting the flag on the loader bail ([#1284](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1284)).
- **`coco init` now persists the recommended `.coco.json` config.** Choosing the recommended `.coco.json` project-config format previously wrote nothing while still reporting success (only the legacy `.coco.config.json` was handled). Both JSON formats are now written, with a defensive guard so an unhandled format fails loudly instead of silently ([#1285](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1285)).
- **`coco init` model picker: corrected the o-series ids.** The OpenAI model list had `o3` / `o3-mini` mistyped as `03` / `03-mini` (digit zero) and a duplicate `gpt-4.1`, so the picker offered non-existent ids and validation didn't recognize the real ones. Fixed and deduped ([#1286](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1286)).
- Docs: the README now leads with a `coco commit` hero GIF pointed at a real code change ([#1267](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1267)).

## Under the hood

- LangChain internals: dropped a dead `llm` param and tightened `createSchemaParser`'s return type ([#1269](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1269)); unified the transient "is-retryable-error" notion into one shared helper ([#1270](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1270)).
- Flag-alias guard broadened to assert no within-command short-flag collision across all command configs, and redundant `CommitOptions` casts dropped ([#1287](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1287)).
- The decomposition above is contributor-facing only: each cluster was lifted verbatim into a hook called at its original slot (preserving React hook order), validated per-PR with `tsc` + the workstation render-snapshot suite + `eslint` + a full build.

## Breaking Changes

- **Two short-flag aliases were removed** to end conflicting letters ([#1268](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1268)):
  - `coco commit -t` no longer resolves — use the long form **`--appendTicket`** (`-t` is now `--tag` on `coco changelog`).
  - `coco log -c` no longer resolves — use the long form **`--commit`** (`-c` is now `--conventional` on `coco commit`).

  The long flags are unchanged; only the ambiguous short letters moved. A `flagAliasConsistency.test.ts` guard prevents regressions.

Otherwise behavior-preserving — the workstation runtime decomposition is internal (zero render-snapshot diffs), and existing configs and TUI flows are unchanged.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/gfargo/coco/compare/0.72.0...0.72.1

## What's Changed

`0.72.0` is primarily an under-the-hood release. There are **no new commands, flags, or changes to how the CLI behaves** — the `coco ui` workstation looks and behaves exactly as it did in `0.71.0`. The headline work is a large, behavior-preserving refactor that breaks the workstation's monolithic runtime component into focused, testable pieces. Alongside it, this release makes `coco` **easier to install** (Homebrew + a `curl` one-liner) and adds a **release-safety guard**. It's a drop-in upgrade.

## Highlights

### The workstation runtime, decomposed

`src/workstation/runtime/app.ts` — the single React component behind `coco ui` — had grown to **5,368 lines**. This release decomposes it into **26 focused hook modules**, landed across 18 separately-reviewed, individually-green pull requests:

- **app.ts: 5,368 → 1,804 lines (−66%)**
- `useEffect` 41 → 15, `useCallback` ~41 → 6
- Each cluster — filtered lists, status-surface data, idle-tip / spinner / auto-dismiss timers, repo persistence, the on-demand detail/diff/context hydration loaders, cursor-sync + load-more pagination, and the whole action layer (staging, compose/editor, commit-split, AI-draft, pull-request, yank/changelog, and the ~1,200-line workflow dispatcher) — now lives in its own `use*` hook with its own focused unit tests.

### Why it matters

- **Maintainability:** the runtime is now a thin component that wires together named, single-responsibility hooks instead of one 5k-line file. Future workstation features land in (or next to) a small hook rather than the monolith.
- **Testability:** the pure cores of each cluster (filter logic, spinner/idle cadence, hydration guards, pagination math) are now unit-tested in isolation.
- **A foundation for less prop-drilling:** a `LogInkRuntimeContext` provider (installed in an earlier release) now has its **first real consumer** — the header surface reads `state` / `context` / `theme` / `layout` from context instead of receiving them as positional props. Other surfaces can migrate onto it incrementally.

### Easier to install

`npm install -g git-coco` is no longer the only way in. `0.72.0` adds two lower-friction paths ([#1250](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1250)):

- **Homebrew** — the zero-prerequisite path. Homebrew pulls in Node as a dependency, so you don't need a Node toolchain first:

  ```bash
  brew install gfargo/tap/coco
  ```

- **`curl` installer** — checks for Node 22+, installs `git-coco` with whatever package manager you have (npm/pnpm/yarn), and prints next steps. Pin a version with `COCO_VERSION`:

  ```bash
  curl -fsSL https://coco.griffen.codes/install.sh | sh
  ```

The README now leads with the core flow — `git add . && coco commit` across seven providers including fully-local Ollama — with the workstation reframed as the "grows into" payoff ([#1251](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1251)).

## Notable

- **Behavior-preserving by construction.** Every effect and callback was moved byte-for-byte — bodies and dependency arrays unchanged, hook call-order preserved, multi-region clusters split into position-preserving hooks rather than reordered. The on-demand hydration loaders keep their frame-tagging and cancellation semantics exactly; the AI-draft / pull-request abort handles and `mountedRef` unmount guards are reproduced verbatim.
- **Verified.** The full suite (3,471 tests across 276 suites) and the type-checker pass on every step, across the Node 22/24 × Linux/macOS/Windows CI matrix. A post-merge audit (structural integrity, a byte-for-byte behavior diff of the highest-risk extractions, and a security read of the extracted action + spawn paths) found **no regressions** and no must-fix items.
- **One hardening fix rode along.** The commit-split flow's diagnostic dump (repo metadata written to `/tmp` for the silent-failure debugging aid) now lands in an `mkdtemp` directory with `0o600` perms instead of a predictable, world-readable, timestamp-named path — matching the editor temp-file hooks. User-invisible; closes a low-severity info-leak / symlink-redirect risk on shared hosts ([#1236](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1236)).
- **Releases are now guarded against no-op publishes.** A new `release:verify` step (wired into the release flow) builds, packs, and diffs the local `dist/` against the latest published tarball, aborting if they're byte-identical or the version already exists on npm — the exact failure mode behind the `0.70.0` incident. `release-it`'s pre-release pull is also hardened to `--ff-only` ([#1252](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1252)).

## Under the hood

- 26 new `src/workstation/runtime/hooks/use*.ts` modules; the runtime component now composes them.
- Header surface migrated from a render function to a memoized `React.memo` component consuming `LogInkRuntimeContext` — the first step of a gradual surface→context migration.
- Added `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` (rules-of-hooks as error, exhaustive-deps as warning) — a lint safety net for the newly-extracted hooks and future runtime work ([#1235](https://github.com/gfargo/coco/pull/1235)).
- New distribution tooling: `install.sh` (curl installer), `packaging/homebrew/coco.rb` (canonical formula), and `bin/genHomebrewFormula.mjs` / `bin/verifyRelease.mjs` with `release:formula` / `release:verify` npm scripts.

## Breaking Changes

None.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/gfargo/coco/compare/0.71.0...0.72.0
